verdict.rationale: Semgrep Code is documented as a SAST tool. Its taint-tracking rules are explicitly described as catching complex injection bugs such as XSS, and cross-file analysis extends detection across files. Community users confirm using it for security lint rules and curated per-language rulesets, though hands-on reports show simple pattern rules can miss aliasing workarounds. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of out-of-the-box injection/XSS rulesets (taint evidence centers on writing rules), and independent corroboration specifically of injection/XSS detection accuracy.

support.subject: As a developer, I can run static analysis that finds vulnerability classes like injection and XSS in my source code

citations.quote: Semgrep Code is a static application security testing (SAST) tool that
Taint tracking (known also as taint analysis) enables you to write simple rules that catch complex injection bugs, such as those that can result in cross-site scripting (XSS).
To turn on cross-file analysis, which allows you to detect vulnerabilities across files and folders
semgrep scan - This is the recommended command for scanning local codebases or scanning a project when you don't have a Semgrep account
